intro: Fully funded four-year CRUK Manchester Institute PhD in leukaemia biology, October 2027 intake. Tax-free stipend GBP 21,113-23,294 per year plus fees. Deadline: 6 November 2026, 17:00 GMT.
description:
About the Position

The Cancer Research UK Manchester Institute (CRUK MI) is recruiting a PhD student for a four-year fully funded studentship in leukaemia biology. The studentship is based at the Institute's research campus and starts in October 2027 as part of the CRUK MI PhD Programme.

CRUK MI is a cancer research institute in partnership with The University of Manchester, combining discovery science with translational research. The Leukaemia Biology group studies the molecular and cellular mechanisms driving leukaemia and blood cancers, and the successful applicant will join a supportive, well-funded research environment with access to state-of-the-art facilities and cores.

Research Areas

  • Molecular mechanisms of leukaemia
  • Normal and malignant haematopoiesis
  • Disease modelling and drug response
  • Genomic and cellular assays

Funding and Support

Studentship funding
ComponentDetails
StipendGBP 21,113 in year 1; GBP 22,500 in year 2; GBP 22,894 in year 3; GBP 23,294 in year 4 (tax-free annual stipend), with tuition fees covered.
FeesUniversity tuition fees covered in full (home eligibility; check the official page for international-fee terms).
DurationFour-year PhD studentship starting October 2027.
TrainingCRUK MI doctoral training including scientific courses, seminars and career development.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationA bachelor's or master's degree (or expected award) in a relevant life science, biomedical or related subject - see the project page for the exact requirements.
Research interestDemonstrable interest in cancer research and the project's scientific area; prior lab or computational experience is valuable.
EnglishEvidence of English language proficiency per The University of Manchester postgraduate admission requirements.

About University of Manchester

The University of Manchester is a public research university in Manchester, England, and a member of the Russell Group. It offers undergraduate, master's and doctoral programmes across engineering, science, medicine, business and the humanities. Its research community connects academic discovery with challenges in health, sustainability, technology and society through collaboration.

Official website: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/

Application dates

Recruitment information
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline6 November 2026, 17:00 GMT
IntakeOctober 2027
LocationCRUK Manchester Institute, Manchester, United Kingdom

How to Apply

Apply before the deadline on 6th November 2026 at 17:00 GMT through the official CRUK MI application portal (linked from the project page). Applications typically require a CV, academic transcripts, a personal statement and referee contact details.

Official Link

  • Official advert and application (verified link)
  • Submit a PhD studentship application (official CRUK MI portal)
  • CRUK Manchester Institute PhD programme (official)

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: 6 November 2026, 17:00 GMT - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.
